title: Protocol for quantitative analysis of pulsatile contractions and cell extrusion in epithelial tissues of larval zebrafish
protocol: Prepare MTZ solution.
Add solution to larvae at a final concentration of 10 mM and pipette well to avoid crystallization.
Incubate at 28°C for 2 h in the dark.
Add 5–7 drops of tricaine/well to anesthetize larvae.
Transfer larvae using a glass pipet into a dry 35 mm glass bottom dish.
Add a drop of tricaine to the dish for 10–20 seconds.
Remove excess liquid around larvae.
Pipette 100 μL of 0.5% agarose onto the larvae.
Center larvae in agarose under a routine stereo microscope.
Mount larvae so that both dorsal-ventral and anterior-posterior axes are visible, ensuring the edge of the tail appears flat.
Reposition larvae so that they remain completely flat until agarose starts to solidify.
Wait for agarose to become opaque when fully solidified.
Add a drop of tricaine once the agarose is solidified.
Complete with 1 mL of E3 solution.
Acquire Z-stack images using a laser-scanning confocal microscope.
Use either a 20× air objective or a 40× water objective depending on desired x-y resolution.
Adjust z-step from 1 to 3 μm based on the area being acquired.
Ensure time-step does not exceed 30 seconds for in-depth analysis of pulsing events.
Generate maximum intensity projections for all captured z-stack files.
Save maximum intensity projections in 8-bit Tiff file format.
Split the time-lapse Tiff file into individual images representing each time point.
Open the Tissue Analyzer plugin in Fiji and drag image sequences into the “Image List” box.
In the “Segmentation” section, click “Detect Bonds” and set parameters.
Adjust parameters such as the minimum size of desired detected cells.
Process all images at once by clicking “Detect Bonds (save watershed)” to generate segmented images of epithelial cells.
Split Tiff file into image sequences.
Load image sequences in PIVlab.
Add and import images.
Select the region of interest that will be analyzed in Exclusion (ROI, Mask).
Exclude any cells that are not fluorescently tagged in the image analysis.
Adjust image fluorescence during pre-processing.
Apply CLAHE, highpass, and denoise filters to images.
Set passes and interrogation windows: 128 × 128, 64 × 64, 32 × 32, and 16 × 16 pixel-size with 50% overlap each.
Analyze the images in the analysis section once settings are applied.
Calibrate images by inserting time interval and scale after completion of PIV analysis for all frames.
Correct mistakes in the analysis using post-processing options if necessary.
Select velocity limits during post-processing to refine analysis results.
